newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia expels suspected criminal to Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia expels suspected criminal to Shanghai.

text.p: Cambodia has expelled a Chinese national wanted on charges of rape and armed robbery in Shanghai, a senior police officer said on Monday.
Police General Skadavy M. Ly Roun said police arrested Zhang Qiang-sia on Friday and he was escorted back to Shanghai on Sunday by four Chinese officers.
"The one Chinese we expelled from Cambodia is wanted by Interpol China...He's wanted by the police in Shanghai, he's wanted for rape and armed robbery," the general told Reuters.
He said Zhang, who was found carrying two passports in different names, was arrested with more than 80 ethnic Chinese in a December 25 raid on a Phnom Penh villa.
Most of the other Chinese were deported, but Zhang was released on a court order as he was travelling on a valid visa.
"We didn't know he was wanted by Interpol China," Skadavy said.

Two Hong Kong nationals, who were in the house, were also arrested for their suspected involvement in a smuggling ring that is believed to have illegally moved mainland Chinese to the United States, South America, Europe and Africa.
They are expected to be taken to court for immigration offences and deported to Hong Kong, Skadavy said, adding that he had asked Hong Kong police to send arrest warrants.
